description: Official Quality Assurance Committee (QAC) SO/PI assessment rubrics extracted verbatim from the byte-preserved QAC Excel templates. Contains no suggested assignments, CLO interpretation or instructional guidance. SO and PI identifiers refer to abet.student_outcomes and abet.performance_indicators in ee_curriculum.json, which remain the single source of truth; SO/PI descriptions are not duplicated here (only the QAC criterion label is kept, for fidelity).

authority.authoritative_sheets: The visible rubric sheet(s) of each workbook (see rubrics[].source). Hidden legacy sheets are not extracted.
authority.text_policy: All text fields are verbatim cell values (including non-breaking spaces, bullets and typographical errors). Nothing is corrected.

criteria.label: PI11 Identify the key requirements, interacting variables, and technical issues of a complex engineering problem

above.text: Correctly identifies the key requirements, interacting variables, and relevant technical issues, and clearly demonstrates their significance to the engineering problem.

meet.text: Correctly identifies the key requirements, main interacting variables, and relevant technical issues of the engineering problem.

developing.text: Identifies some relevant requirements, variables, or technical issues, but important elements are missing, unclear, or incorrectly identified.

below.text: Key requirements, interacting variables, and technical issues are missing, incorrect, or not relevant to the engineering problem.

checklists.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Are the key requirements, interacting variables, and relevant technical issues identified?
• Are important interactions between variables explained?
• Are the identified technical issues relevant to the engineering problem?
Individual Assessment:
• Identify one important interaction between variables and one key technical issue, and explain their significance to the problem.

segments.heading: Team assessment (Report):
segments.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Are the key requirements, interacting variables, and relevant technical issues identified?
• Are important interactions between variables explained?
• Are the identified technical issues relevant to the engineering problem?

segments.heading: Individual Assessment:
segments.text:
Individual Assessment:
• Identify one important interaction between variables and one key technical issue, and explain their significance to the problem.

checklists.text: Does the student identify the key requirements, interacting variables, and relevant technical issues of the complex engineering problem?

segments.text: Does the student identify the key requirements, interacting variables, and relevant technical issues of the complex engineering problem?

criteria.label: PI12  Formulate an engineering or mathematical model of a complex engineering problem using appropriate assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships.

above.text: Formulates a complete and coherent engineering or mathematical model using appropriate assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships, and clearly justifies key modeling choices.

meet.text: Formulates an appropriate engineering or mathematical model using relevant assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships sufficient to represent the engineering problem.

developing.text: Formulates a partial model, but important assumptions, parameters, or governing relationships are missing, unclear, or incorrectly represented.

below.text: An appropriate engineering or mathematical model is missing, incorrect, or does not adequately represent the engineering problem.

checklists.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Is an appropriate engineering or mathematical model formulated?
• Are the important assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships identified?
• Do the governing relationships represent the important behavior/interactions in the problem?
Individual Assessment:
• Explain one important assumption, parameter, or governing relationship in the model and why it is appropriate.

segments.heading: Team assessment (Report):
segments.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Is an appropriate engineering or mathematical model formulated?
• Are the important assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships identified?
• Do the governing relationships represent the important behavior/interactions in the problem?

segments.heading: Individual Assessment:
segments.text:
Individual Assessment:
• Explain one important assumption, parameter, or governing relationship in the model and why it is appropriate.

checklists.text: Does the student formulate an appropriate engineering or mathematical model using suitable assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships?

segments.text: Does the student formulate an appropriate engineering or mathematical model using suitable assumptions, parameters, and governing relationships?

criteria.label: PI13  Solve the formulated complex engineering problem by applying appropriate principles of engineering, science, and mathematics using suitable analytical, computational, or experimental methods.

above.text: Correctly applies appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles using a suitable analytical, computational, or experimental method to obtain a valid solution, and demonstrates sound engineering judgment in applying and interpreting the solution method.

meet.text: Correctly applies appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles using a suitable analytical, computational, or experimental method to obtain a valid solution.

developing.text: Applies some appropriate principles or methods, but the solution is incomplete or contains significant errors in method, calculations, implementation, or interpretation.

below.text: Appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles are not applied, the selected method is inappropriate, or no valid solution is obtained.

checklists.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Are appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles applied?
• Is a suitable analytical, computational, or experimental method used?
• Is the solution technically correct and sufficiently complete?
Individual Assessment:
• Explain the method used to solve the problem, why it was appropriate, and one important step in obtaining the solution.

segments.heading: Team assessment (Report):
segments.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Are appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles applied?
• Is a suitable analytical, computational, or experimental method used?
• Is the solution technically correct and sufficiently complete?

segments.heading: Individual Assessment:
segments.text:
Individual Assessment:
• Explain the method used to solve the problem, why it was appropriate, and one important step in obtaining the solution.

checklists.text: Does the student correctly apply appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles and a suitable analytical, computational, or experimental method to obtain a valid solution?

segments.text: Does the student correctly apply appropriate engineering, science, and mathematics principles and a suitable analytical, computational, or experimental method to obtain a valid solution?

assessment_note.text:
Assessment Note: 
• Team-based assessment is based on team evidence (e.g., final report).
• Individual attainment may be verified through structured oral questions or individual exam questions.
• Use the checklist column(s) applicable to the selected assessment method; non-applicable checklist items may be left unused.
• For project-based assessment with oral individual verification, use the project checklist. For project-based assessment with individual exam verification, use both the project and exam checklists. For exam-only assessment, use the exam checklist.

criteria.label: PI31 – Communicate engineering information using appropriate technical content

above.text: Communicates relevant and sufficient engineering information with appropriate technical content, explanation, and supporting evidence.

meet.text: Communicates generally relevant engineering information with sufficient technical content and explanation.

developing.text: Communicates limited or incomplete engineering information; important technical content or explanation is missing.

below.text: Communicates little or no meaningful engineering information.

checklists.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Is the essential engineering information included? 
• Are key concepts/results explained? 
• Is the technical detail sufficient? Is terminology appropriate? 
Are conclusions supported by evidence/results?

Individual Assessment:
• Does the student clearly explain his/her assigned technical content?
• Can the student answer related technical questions?

criteria.label: PI32 – Use appropriate communication methods and engineering representations to effectively convey information..

above.text: Selects and effectively uses appropriate communication methods (presentation, report, poster, demo, etc.) and engineering representations (figures, tables, Schematics, block diagrams, plots, flowchart, etc.) that clearly enhance understanding of the information.

meet.text: Uses appropriate communication forms and engineering representations that adequately convey the information.

developing.text: Uses limited, unclear, or poorly selected communication forms or engineering representations.

below.text: Fails to use appropriate communication forms or engineering representations, making the information difficult to understand.

checklists.text:
Team assessment (Report):
• Are the chosen forms appropriate? Are plots/figures/schematics/tables suitable and readable? 
• Are axes, units, legends, and captions provided where needed? 
• Are visuals referenced/explained? Do the representations improve understanding?

Individual Assessment:
• Does the student effectively use and explain the representations in his/her assigned part?
• Are the selected visuals/representations appropriate for the information being presented?

below.text: Communication shows little or no consideration of the intended audience.

criteria.label: PI42 – Make informed judgments considering the impact of engineering solutions in global, societal, economic, and environmental contexts

meet.text: Makes an appropriate informed judgment by considering and explaining the main relevant impacts in applicable contexts.

developing.text: Makes a limited judgment; some relevant impacts are identified, but analysis or justification is incomplete.

below.text: Does not make a meaningful informed judgment; relevant impacts are missing, incorrect, or not connected to the judgment.

• Does the analysis support a clear engineering judgment or decision?

notes.text:
Notes: 
-PI results are calculated as the percentage of students who achieved a score of 2 or 3. 
-The SO result is calculated as the percentage of students whose average PI score is 2.0 or higher.
-When both project and individual assessments are used, the final PI score is determined based on the combined evidence (average) from both assessments.
